chunks.label: Feeling unwell
chunks.rationale: Say you're not feeling well and why.
chunks.interference: Choushi and guai both mean 'condition'; guai leans toward feeling physically ill.

chunks.label: School classes
chunks.rationale: Talk about classes, tests and homework.
chunks.interference: Kumi and kurasu both mean a class; teishutsu is the formal word for dasu (hand in).

chunks.label: Work hours and time off
chunks.rationale: Talk about your workday, overtime and days off.
chunks.interference: Kyuukei (a short break), yuukyuu (paid leave) and renkyuu (days off in a row) all sound alike.

chunks.label: Doctors and medicine
chunks.rationale: Get help for an illness: medicine, doctors, tests and treatment.
chunks.interference: Kensa is a medical test, not a school tesuto.

chunks.label: Injuries and emergencies
chunks.rationale: Handle an accident: who got hurt and who to call.
chunks.interference: Kega is the injury, kizu the visible cut or mark.

chunks.label: Symptoms and seasonal ills
chunks.rationale: Describe common symptoms and the seasonal ills everyone talks about.
chunks.interference: Netchuushou (heatstroke) shares its first sound with netsu (fever) but is a different thing.

chunks.label: Staying healthy
chunks.rationale: Talk about health habits, exercise, weight and check-ups.
chunks.interference: Daietto only means trying to lose weight, never your normal diet.

chunks.label: Meetings and deadlines
chunks.rationale: Handle the office calendar: meetings, papers, trips and deadlines.
chunks.interference: Uchiawase is a working meeting; kaigi is a formal one.

chunks.label: In and out of hospital
chunks.rationale: Share news about hospital stays, operations, recovery and pregnancy.
chunks.interference: Nyuuin (go in) and taiin (come out) are easy to swap.

chunks.label: Jobs and business
chunks.rationale: Say what work you do and who you work with.
chunks.interference: Eigyou (sales) and shoubai (trade, running a shop) both come out as 'business' in English.

chunks.label: Rules and permission
chunks.rationale: Say what's allowed, what's banned and what's your right.

chunks.label: Projects and results
chunks.rationale: Talk a project through from idea to the big day and how it was rated.
chunks.interference: Kikaku (a proposal to make something) is not keikaku (a plan in general).

chunks.label: Society and the news
chunks.rationale: Comment on the news and how the world works.
chunks.interference: Jiken (incident, crime) gets mixed up with jiko (accident); yo no naka and shakai overlap.

chunks.label: Skills and expertise
chunks.rationale: Say what you research, specialise in or work with.
chunks.interference: Kenkyuu is research, not everyday studying (benkyou).

chunks.label: Big topics
chunks.rationale: Talk about the environment, history and education.
